narrative: With a high pressure system extending from northwest of the Great Lakes east-southeast across Northern New England, a low pressure system developed off the Carolina Coast during Thursday evening on November 13th.  It slowly intensified as it moved northeast, passing south of Long Island during Friday afternoon before moving offshore during Friday evening.Northeast gales developed over the coastal waters around 2:00 am Friday morning and continued until around noon.  Sustained wind speeds reached 38 knots at the Ambrose Light Tower Bouy and 33 knots at Bouy 44025.  Significant wave heights rose sharply to around 11 ft at Ambrose and to around 17 ft at Bouy 44025 at noon Friday.A combination of strong northeast winds, high astronomical tides and high waves caused minor to moderate coastal flooding across the area.  The most significant flooding occurred across the shores of Nassau County.  Up to 2 feet of water was in several streets in Freeport, where some vehicles suffered water damage.  Water not only rose above the bulk head but also came up through the storm drains in Bayville, where several pumps were used to drain a four block area.  Street flooding along with moderate beach erosion was common along the shores.
